owned_invariants: The task may declare sources, an object of texts, and inputs, an object in which each value names a registered domain checker and gives an input object. Anything else under those keys is refused before a prompt is written.
The reply is a nonempty list of claims, each an object with a text id, no id twice, and optionally a list of the ids it says are admitted.

An exact claim is checked only against an input the task declares, by the checker the task chose for that input, on the claim's witness. A claim that names no declared input, or that brings an input or a checker of its own, fails and is not run.

A quote claim on a declared source with a span list is checked by bytes: it holds when start < end, the span lies inside the source, and the bytes of the span are the bytes of the quoted text. The witness is the SHA-256 of the source's canonical JSON text and the span.

A claim of any other kind, a quote with no declared source or no span list, and the free text on a claim that is not a quote have no check. They are never admitted and are named as open obligations, on a certified run and on a refused one.

Each checked claim is bound to the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the claim and the host's witness, where the claim leaves out its stated digest and, unless it is a quote, its free text. A claim that states a digest must state that one.

The run is refused when a checked claim fails, when a stated digest is not the host's, when the reply lists as admitted an id the host did not admit, or when nothing is admitted. Otherwise it is certified with the admitted ids and their digests: ALL_CLAIMS_ADMITTED when nothing is open, CLAIM_SCOPED when something is.
boundaries: Admission means the claim passed its own check on its own evidence. An admitted exact claim says nothing about the claim's free text, which stays open.
A quote check shows the text is in the source at that span. It does not show the source supports what the reply says about it.
Spans are byte offsets into the source as UTF-8.
A digest covers the claim as written: a number with a fraction or an exponent is hashed as its own text.
